I can see a corn plant with an exposed ear showing poor kernel fill - scattered, sparse, pale kernels with gaps. The plant has dried/brown leaves. This suggests systemic disease affecting ear development.

Top candidates: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma (loose tooth ears, stunting), Head_smut, Ear_rots_Diplodia. Let me check references.
Head_smut shows black spore masses - not matching. Diplodia shows white mold - not matching. Let me check more candidates.

None of those match well. The test image shows an ear with very poor kernel fill (bare cob at tip, sparse loose kernels), which is characteristic of Corn Stunt Spiroplasma's "loose tooth ears." Let me check one more reference.

Misc doesn't match. My **initial prediction is Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** based on the poor kernel fill, bare cob tip, sparse loose kernels ("loose tooth ears"), and dried plant.

Now let me check the attractor guide per step 5.

Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma is listed as over-predicted (3x wrong), with alternatives being Crazy_top (2x) and Ear_rots_Aspergillus (1x). I already viewed Crazy_top (bushy tassel replacement - not matching) and Ear_rots_Aspergillus would show green mold. Neither fits this image.

The test image clearly shows:
- An ear with very poor kernel fill and bare cob at the tip
- Sparse, loose-looking pale kernels ("loose tooth" appearance)
- Dried/dead plant with brown leaves
- Overall stressed/stunted plant

This matches Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma's hallmark symptoms: "loose tooth ears" with blank spaces, poor kernel fill, and premature plant death.
